From 1887 Kate Sheppard, the WCTU's franchise superintendent, wrote pamphlets, lobbied members of parliament and organised petitions. In 1891 and 1892 bills passed the lower house but failed in the appointed Legislative Council.

In 1893 the petition grew to nearly 32,000 signatures, perhaps a quarter of the adult women in the colony, pasted end to end on a roll some 270 metres long. When it was unrolled down the floor of the debating chamber in July, it struck parliament with its sheer length. Premier Richard Seddon opposed the bill and tried to defeat it by procedure, but two councillors changed their votes in protest at his tactics, and it passed 20 to 18.

Women enrolled in their tens of thousands, and on 28 November more than 90,000 women, over 80 per cent of those enrolled, cast a vote. That same year Elizabeth Yates became mayor of Onehunga, the first woman mayor in the British Empire. Sheppard's face is on the New Zealand ten-dollar note.
story.zh:
选举权运动源自禁酒运动：女性希望借助选票遏制毁掉家庭的酒类贸易。从1887年起，基督教妇女禁酒联合会选举权负责人凯特·谢泼德撰写小册子、游说议员、组织请愿。1891年和1892年，相关法案在下院获得通过，却在任命制的立法会受挫。

1893年，请愿书签名增至近3.2万个，约占殖民地成年女性的四分之一，签名纸首尾相接粘成长约270米的卷轴。7月，卷轴沿辩论厅地板展开，其长度令议会震动。总理理查德·塞登反对该法案，试图以程序手段使其失败，但两名立法会议员为抗议他的手法而改投赞成票，法案以20票对18票通过。

数以万计的女性登记为选民，11月28日有九万多名女性投票，占已登记女性的八成以上。同年，伊丽莎白·耶茨当选奥内洪加市长，成为大英帝国第一位女市长。谢泼德的头像如今印在新西兰十元纸币上。

name.zh: 澳大利亚联邦成立

summary.en: After referendums in the 1890s, the six colonies united as the Commonwealth of Australia, proclaimed in Sydney's Centennial Park on 1 January 1901 with Edmund Barton as prime minister. The constitution excluded Aboriginal people from the census and left them to the states, and the new parliament soon passed the White Australia laws.
summary.zh: 经过19世纪90年代的多次公投，六个殖民地联合为澳大利亚联邦，1901年1月1日在悉尼百年纪念公园宣告成立，埃德蒙·巴顿出任总理。宪法把原住民排除在人口统计之外，并交由各州管理；新议会随即通过了“白澳”诸法。

sources.title: National Archives of Australia: Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act 1900
National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – Federation
H. Irving, To Constitute a Nation: A Cultural History of Australia's Constitution (Cambridge University Press, 1997)

story.en:
In the 1880s the Australian colonies had separate armies, railways of different gauges and tariffs at every border. Fear of foreign powers in the Pacific and of Asian immigration, and the hope of free trade between the colonies, pushed leaders like Henry Parkes, who in 1890 spoke of 'the crimson thread of kinship', toward union.

Conventions in 1891 and 1897–98 drafted a constitution, which voters in the colonies approved in referendums between 1898 and 1900; Western Australia joined last, after goldfields residents threatened to secede. The British parliament passed the Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act in July 1900.

On New Year's Day 1901 a procession of soldiers, unionists and dignitaries wound through Sydney to Centennial Park, where the governor-general, Lord Hopetoun, was sworn in before some 60,000 people. Parliament opened in Melbourne in May. Its early laws, the Immigration Restriction Act and the Pacific Island Labourers Act, built the White Australia policy into the foundations of the nation.
story.zh:
19世纪80年代，澳大利亚各殖民地各有军队，铁路轨距不一，边界处处设关征税。对太平洋上外国势力和亚洲移民的恐惧，以及对殖民地间自由贸易的期望，推动亨利·帕克斯等领导人走向联合；1890年帕克斯曾谈到“血脉相连的红线”。

1891年和1897至1898年的制宪会议起草了宪法，1898至1900年各殖民地选民通过公投予以批准；西澳大利亚在金矿区居民威胁分离后最后加入。1900年7月，英国议会通过《澳大利亚联邦宪法法》。

1901年元旦，由士兵、工会会员和政要组成的游行队伍穿过悉尼前往百年纪念公园，总督霍普顿勋爵在约六万人面前宣誓就职。5月议会在墨尔本开幕。其早期立法《移民限制法》和《太平洋岛民劳工法》把“白澳政策”嵌入了国家的根基。

name.en: Immigration Restriction Act and the White Australia policy
name.zh: 《移民限制法》与“白澳政策”

summary.en: One of the first laws of the new Commonwealth let officials exclude any migrant who failed a dictation test in any European language, a device aimed chiefly at Asians. Together with the deportation of Pacific Islanders it formed the White Australia policy, dismantled in stages from 1949 and formally ended by the Whitlam government in 1973.
summary.zh: 这是新联邦最早的法律之一，允许官员以任何一种欧洲语言进行听写测试，把未通过者拒之门外，这一手段主要针对亚洲人。它与遣返太平洋岛民一起构成“白澳政策”，该政策自1949年起逐步拆除，1973年由惠特拉姆政府正式终结。

sources.title: National Archives of Australia: Immigration Restriction Act 1901
National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – White Australia policy
G. Tavan, The Long, Slow Death of White Australia (Scribe, 2005)

story.en:
Hostility to Chinese miners on the goldfields, and to Pacific Islander and Asian labour in the north, ran through colonial politics in the late 19th century. When the first federal parliament met in Melbourne in 1901, restricting 'coloured' immigration was among its first tasks. Britain objected to an openly racial test that would offend Japan, whose goodwill it was courting, so Edmund Barton's government, with Attorney-General Alfred Deakin steering the bill, adopted a disguised one: officials could give any would-be migrant a fifty-word dictation in any European language they chose.

The test was designed to be failed. In 1934 it was used against the Czech journalist Egon Kisch, who spoke several languages, by testing him in Scottish Gaelic. Non-European residents faced deportation, and families were divided.

After the Second World War Australia took in large numbers of European refugees and migrants, while the Colombo Plan brought Asian students. The dictation test was abolished in 1958, restrictions eased in 1966, and in 1973 the Whitlam government removed race from immigration policy altogether. Refugees from Vietnam arrived later that decade, and Australia's population has since become one of the most diverse in the world.
story.zh:
19世纪后期，对金矿区华人矿工以及北部太平洋岛民和亚洲劳工的敌视贯穿殖民地政治。1901年首届联邦议会在墨尔本开会时，限制“有色人种”移民是其首要任务之一。英国反对公开以种族为标准的测试，因为这会冒犯它正在拉拢的日本，于是巴顿政府在司法部长阿尔弗雷德·迪金主持下采用了一种变相手段：官员可以用其任选的任何一种欧洲语言，对任何申请入境者进行五十个词的听写测试。

这项测试本就是为让人不及格而设计的。1934年，当局对通晓多种语言的捷克记者埃贡·基希使用了苏格兰盖尔语进行测试。非欧洲裔居民面临驱逐，家庭被拆散。

二战后，澳大利亚接纳了大批欧洲难民和移民，“科伦坡计划”则带来了亚洲留学生。听写测试于1958年废除，1966年限制放宽，1973年惠特拉姆政府彻底把种族因素从移民政策中删除。这个十年后期越南难民相继到来，此后澳大利亚人口成为世界上最多元的人口之一。

name.en: Malinowski studies the kula ring in the Trobriands
name.zh: 马林诺夫斯基在特罗布里恩群岛研究库拉圈

summary.en: Living in Omarakana village on Kiriwina, Bronisław Malinowski documented the kula, a ceremonial exchange in which shell necklaces (soulava) travel clockwise and armshells (mwali) anticlockwise around a ring of islands off eastern New Guinea. His Argonauts of the Western Pacific (1922) founded modern ethnographic fieldwork.
summary.zh: 布罗尼斯瓦夫·马林诺夫斯基住在基里维纳岛的奥马拉卡纳村，记录了“库拉”这种仪式性交换：在新几内亚东部外海的一圈岛屿间，贝壳项链（索拉瓦）顺时针流转，贝壳臂环（姆瓦利）逆时针流转。他1922年出版的《西太平洋的航海者》奠定了现代民族志田野调查的方法。

sources.title: B. Malinowski, Argonauts of the Western Pacific (Routledge, 1922)
Britannica: Bronisław Malinowski
J. W. Leach & E. Leach (eds), The Kula: New Perspectives on Massim Exchange (Cambridge University Press, 1983)

note: The kula itself is far older than Malinowski's fieldwork; the dates are those of his Trobriand stays.

name.zh: 首个澳新军团日

summary.en: On the first anniversary of the Gallipoli landings, services and marches were held across Australia and New Zealand and some 2,000 troops marched in London. Promoted in Brisbane by Canon David Garland, the day became a national day of remembrance, with dawn services from the 1920s. The campaign itself is ev-gallipoli-campaign.
summary.zh: 在加里波利登陆一周年之际，澳大利亚和新西兰各地举行纪念仪式和游行，约两千名士兵在伦敦列队行进。经布里斯班的戴维·加兰教士大力推动，这一天成为全国纪念日，自20世纪20年代起举行黎明仪式。战役本身见“加里波利战役”条目。

sources.title: Australian War Memorial: Anzac Day
NZHistory: The first Anzac Day

note: About 8,700 Australians and 2,800 New Zealanders died at Gallipoli; the landing is recorded in the west-asia dataset (ev-gallipoli-campaign).

story.en:
At dawn on 25 April 1915 troops of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps landed at Ari Burnu on the Gallipoli peninsula. Eight months later they were evacuated, having lost about 11,500 dead between them. For two small dominions with populations of about five million and just over one million, the losses were staggering, and the newspapers' accounts of the landing were read as the nations' baptism of fire.

The idea of an annual commemoration came quickly. In Brisbane the Anglican canon David Garland, secretary of the Anzac Day Commemoration Committee formed in January 1916, devised a format of a service, a march and a minute's silence, deliberately inclusive of all denominations. On the first anniversary there were services across both countries, and some 2,000 Australian and New Zealand troops marched through London to a service at Westminster Abbey attended by King George V.

Anzac Day became a public holiday in the 1920s, and dawn services, echoing the hour of the landing, spread from the late 1920s. It now honours all who served in war, including Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander and Māori soldiers whose service was long overlooked.
story.zh:
1915年4月25日黎明，澳大利亚和新西兰陆军军团的部队在加里波利半岛的阿里布尔努登陆。八个月后他们撤离，两国合计阵亡约11500人。对于人口分别约五百万和一百余万的两个小自治领而言，这一损失骇人听闻，报纸对登陆的报道被视为两个国家的“战火洗礼”。

每年纪念的设想很快出现。1916年1月成立的布里斯班澳新军团日纪念委员会秘书、圣公会教士戴维·加兰设计了礼拜、游行和默哀一分钟的仪式形式，刻意兼容各教派。一周年之际，两国各地都举行了纪念活动，约2000名澳新官兵列队穿过伦敦，前往威斯敏斯特教堂参加乔治五世出席的礼拜。

20世纪20年代，澳新军团日成为公共假日；呼应登陆时刻的黎明仪式自20年代末开始普及。如今这一天纪念所有参战者，包括长期被忽视的原住民、托雷斯海峡岛民和毛利士兵。

name.zh: 西萨摩亚的流感大流行

summary.en: The New Zealand administration let the steamer Talune land at Apia with influenza aboard. Within two months about 8,500 people, some 22 per cent of Western Samoa's population, died, one of the worst death rates in the world. American Samoa, which imposed quarantine, had no deaths. New Zealand apologised in 2002.
summary.zh: 新西兰当局允许载有流感病人的“塔卢恩号”轮船在阿皮亚靠岸。两个月内约8500人死亡，约占西萨摩亚人口的22%，是世界上死亡率最高的地区之一。实施检疫的美属萨摩亚则无一人死亡。新西兰于2002年正式道歉。

sources.title: NZHistory: The 1918 influenza pandemic in Samoa
G. W. Rice, Black November: The 1918 Influenza Pandemic in New Zealand (Canterbury University Press, 2nd ed. 2005)

story.en:
New Zealand had seized German Samoa at the start of the First World War, and Colonel Robert Logan governed it as administrator. On 7 November 1918 the Union Steam Ship Company's Talune arrived from Auckland, where influenza was raging. Sick passengers were allowed ashore. Within a week the disease had spread to every village on Upolu and Savaiʻi.

So many people fell ill at once that no one was left to cook, fetch water or bury the dead; survivors described bodies being carried to mass graves by the truckload. Many matai, holders of family titles and keepers of genealogies, died, a loss of knowledge as well as of life. When the governor of American Samoa, which had closed its ports, offered doctors and help, Logan is said to have refused even to answer the radio messages.

A New Zealand commission later found the administration negligent. The epidemic hardened Samoan anger at colonial rule and fed the rise of the Mau. In 2002 Prime Minister Helen Clark apologised in Apia for the epidemic and for later injustices.
story.zh:
第一次世界大战爆发时新西兰占领了德属萨摩亚，由罗伯特·洛根上校任行政长官。1918年11月7日，联合轮船公司的“塔卢恩号”从流感肆虐的奥克兰抵达，患病乘客获准上岸。一周之内，疾病已蔓延到乌波卢岛和萨瓦伊岛的每个村庄。

同时病倒的人太多，以至于无人做饭、打水或埋葬死者；幸存者描述尸体被成车运往乱葬坑。许多马塔伊（家族称号持有者和谱系的守护者）死去，失去的不仅是生命，还有知识。关闭了港口的美属萨摩亚总督提出派医生援助，据说洛根连无线电讯息都不予答复。

新西兰的一个调查委员会后来认定当局失职。这场疫情加深了萨摩亚人对殖民统治的愤怒，推动了马乌运动的兴起。2002年，新西兰总理海伦·克拉克在阿皮亚为这场疫情和此后的种种不公正式道歉。

name.zh: 马乌运动与“黑色星期六”

summary.en: The Mau ('firm opinion'), a non-violent movement of Samoan chiefs and some part-European merchants, boycotted New Zealand's administration and demanded self-rule. On 28 December 1929, Black Saturday, police fired on a Mau procession in Apia, killing its leader Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III and ten others. The movement persisted and paved the way to independence.
summary.zh: 马乌运动（意为“坚定的意见”）是萨摩亚酋长和部分欧裔混血商人发起的非暴力运动，抵制新西兰当局并要求自治。1929年12月28日“黑色星期六”，警察向阿皮亚的马乌游行队伍开枪，打死领袖图普阿·塔马塞塞·莱阿洛菲三世等十一人。运动坚持下来，为日后独立铺平了道路。

sources.title: NZHistory: Black Saturday in Samoa
M. Field, Mau: Samoa's Struggle for Freedom (Polynesian Press, rev. ed. 1991)
Britannica: Samoa – History

note: Earlier Mau protests, led by Lauaki Namulauʻulu Mamoe against German rule, date to 1908; this record covers the movement against New Zealand.

story.en:
Administrator George Richardson ruled Western Samoa in the 1920s with paternal zeal, banishing chiefs who defied him and interfering with the bestowal of matai titles. In 1926 the merchant Olaf Nelson helped launch the Mau, whose members wore a uniform of purple lavalava with a white stripe and refused to pay taxes or cooperate with officials.

Nelson was exiled, and Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III, holder of one of the four paramount titles, took the lead. In 1928 he too was deported and jailed in New Zealand. He returned in 1929, and on 28 December he led a procession through Apia to welcome back another exile. When police tried to arrest a man in the crowd, scuffles broke out and police fired, some with a machine gun from the station balcony. Tamasese, shot while calling for calm, died that night; tradition records his plea that no more blood be spilt.

The men of the Mau took to the bush, the women kept the movement alive, and in 1936 a new Labour government in Wellington recognised it. In 2002 New Zealand apologised for the killings.
story.zh:
20世纪20年代，行政长官乔治·理查森以家长式的热情统治西萨摩亚，流放违抗他的酋长，并干预马塔伊称号的授予。1926年，商人奥拉夫·纳尔逊协助发起马乌运动，成员身着饰有白色条纹的紫色围裙作为制服，拒绝纳税和与官员合作。

纳尔逊被流放后，萨摩亚四大最高称号之一的持有者图普阿·塔马塞塞·莱阿洛菲三世接过领导权。1928年他也被驱逐并关押于新西兰。1929年他回国，12月28日率领游行队伍穿过阿皮亚，迎接另一位被流放者归来。警察试图在人群中逮捕一人，引发推搡，警察随即开枪，有人从警署阳台上用机枪扫射。正在呼吁众人冷静的塔马塞塞中弹，当夜身亡；传统记载了他请求不要再流血的遗言。

马乌的男人们退入丛林，女人们则使运动延续下去；1936年惠灵顿新上台的工党政府承认了这一运动。2002年新西兰为这次杀戮道歉。

name.zh: 原住民“哀悼日”

summary.en: While Sydney celebrated 150 years since the First Fleet, about a hundred Aboriginal people met at the Australian Hall in Elizabeth Street for a Day of Mourning and Protest, organised by William Cooper, Jack Patten and William Ferguson. They demanded full citizenship and equality, one of the first national Aboriginal civil rights protests.
summary.zh: 在悉尼庆祝第一舰队抵达150周年之际，约一百名原住民聚集在伊丽莎白街的澳大利亚礼堂，参加由威廉·库珀、杰克·帕滕和威廉·弗格森组织的“哀悼与抗议日”。他们要求完全的公民权与平等，这是最早的全国性原住民民权抗议之一。

sources.title: National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – Day of Mourning
AIATSIS: Day of Mourning 1938

name.zh: 达尔文大轰炸

summary.en: Four days after Singapore fell, 242 Japanese aircraft from the carrier fleet that had struck Pearl Harbor and from land bases attacked Darwin in two raids, sinking eight ships in the harbour and killing at least 235 people. It was the largest attack ever on Australia, the first of about a hundred raids on the north.
summary.zh: 新加坡陷落四天后，来自曾袭击珍珠港的航母舰队及陆上基地的242架日本飞机分两波轰炸达尔文，击沉港内八艘船，至少235人遇难。这是澳大利亚遭受过的最大规模攻击，也是此后对北部约一百次空袭中的第一次。

sources.title: Australian War Memorial: Bombing of Darwin
P. Grose, An Awkward Truth: The Bombing of Darwin, February 1942 (Allen & Unwin, 2009)

name.zh: 科科达小径战役

summary.en: Japanese forces landed at Buna and Gona in July 1942 and pushed over the Owen Stanley Range toward Port Moresby. Outnumbered Australian militia and AIF troops fought a fighting withdrawal along the Kokoda Track, supported by thousands of Papuan carriers, until the Japanese turned back within sight of the town in September. Kokoda was retaken in November.
summary.zh: 1942年7月，日军在布纳和戈纳登陆，翻越欧文斯坦利山脉向莫尔兹比港推进。兵力处于劣势的澳大利亚民兵和澳大利亚帝国军沿科科达小径且战且退，并得到数千名巴布亚搬运工的支援，直到9月日军在能望见该城的地方撤退。11月澳军收复科科达。

label.zh: 约里拜瓦：日军最远推进点

sources.title: Australian War Memorial: Kokoda Track campaign
P. Ham, Kokoda (HarperCollins, 2004)
Department of Veterans' Affairs: The Kokoda Track

story.en:
After the Battle of the Coral Sea turned back a seaborne invasion in May 1942, Japan tried to take Port Moresby overland. On 21 July troops of the South Seas Force landed near Gona and advanced up the track, a footpath through jungle, mud and razor-backed ridges more than 2,000 metres high. The first defenders were young militiamen of the 39th Battalion and the Papuan Infantry Battalion.

At Isurava in late August the outnumbered Australians held for four days before withdrawing; Private Bruce Kingsbury won a posthumous Victoria Cross there. Each retreat stretched the attackers' supply line. By mid-September the Japanese reached Ioribaiwa, about 40 km from Port Moresby, starving and sick, and were ordered back because of the crisis on Guadalcanal.

The campaign could not have been fought without Papuan carriers, who hauled supplies up and carried the wounded down; Australian soldiers called them 'Fuzzy Wuzzy Angels'. Many were conscripted and their contribution was long under-recognised. About 625 Australians died on the track, and many more in the bloody battles at Buna and Gona that followed.
story.zh:
1942年5月珊瑚海海战挫败了日军的海上入侵后，日本企图从陆路夺取莫尔兹比港。7月21日，南海支队在戈纳附近登陆，沿小径推进。这条小径穿越丛林、泥沼和海拔两千多米的刀脊山岭。最先迎战的是第39营的年轻民兵和巴布亚步兵营。

8月下旬在伊苏拉瓦，兵力处于劣势的澳军坚守四天后撤退；列兵布鲁斯·金斯伯里在此阵亡，追授维多利亚十字勋章。每一次撤退都拉长了进攻者的补给线。到9月中旬，饥病交加的日军抵达距莫尔兹比港约40公里的约里拜瓦，又因瓜达尔卡纳尔岛的危机奉命撤回。

没有巴布亚搬运工，这场战役根本无法进行：他们把补给扛上山，把伤员抬下来，澳大利亚士兵称他们为“卷发天使”。许多人是被强征的，他们的贡献长期未获充分承认。约625名澳大利亚人死在小径上，随后布纳和戈纳的血战中死者更多。

name.zh: 瓜达尔卡纳尔岛战役

summary.en: US Marines landed on Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands to seize a Japanese airfield, renamed Henderson Field. Six months of land, sea and air battles followed, with heavy naval losses in 'Ironbottom Sound', until Japan evacuated its last troops in February 1943. Solomon Islander scouts and coastwatchers were vital to the Allied victory.
summary.zh: 美国海军陆战队在所罗门群岛的瓜达尔卡纳尔岛登陆，夺取一座日军机场，改名亨德森机场。随后六个月里陆海空战斗不断，“铁底湾”中双方海军损失惨重，直到1943年2月日本撤出最后的部队。所罗门岛民侦察兵和海岸瞭望员对盟军胜利至关重要。

sources.title: Naval History and Heritage Command: Guadalcanal campaign
R. B. Frank, Guadalcanal: The Definitive Account of the Landmark Battle (Random House, 1990)
Britannica: Battle of Guadalcanal

note: The wider Pacific War is recorded in the japan-korea dataset (ev-pacific-war).

story.en:
In mid-1942 Japanese engineers began building an airfield on Guadalcanal that could threaten the sea lanes between the United States and Australia. On 7 August about 11,000 US Marines landed, took the unfinished strip and named it after a pilot killed at Midway. Two nights later a Japanese cruiser force sank four Allied cruisers off Savo Island, and the transports withdrew, leaving the Marines short of supplies.

For six months both sides fed troops into the island. Japanese destroyers ran reinforcements at night, the 'Tokyo Express', while American aircraft ruled the day. The waters between Guadalcanal, Savo and Florida Island filled with so many wrecks that sailors called them Ironbottom Sound. Disease and hunger killed as many Japanese soldiers as combat did.

Solomon Islanders were drawn into a war not of their making. Coastwatchers with radios on the ridges warned of incoming air raids, and scouts guided patrols; Sergeant Major Jacob Vouza survived torture and bayonet wounds to warn the Marines of an attack. In February 1943 Japan evacuated about 10,000 survivors, and the Allies went on the offensive in the South Pacific.
story.zh:
1942年年中，日本工兵开始在瓜达尔卡纳尔岛修建机场，威胁美澳之间的海上航线。8月7日，约一万一千名美国海军陆战队员登陆，夺取了尚未完工的跑道，并以一位在中途岛阵亡的飞行员命名。两天后的夜里，一支日本巡洋舰编队在萨沃岛附近击沉四艘盟军巡洋舰，运输船随即撤离，陆战队补给告急。

此后六个月，双方不断向岛上投入兵力。日本驱逐舰夜间运送援军，号称“东京快车”，白天则是美军飞机的天下。瓜达尔卡纳尔岛、萨沃岛和佛罗里达岛之间的海域沉船累累，水兵们称之为“铁底湾”。疾病与饥饿造成的日军死亡与战斗伤亡相当。

所罗门岛民被卷入一场并非由他们发动的战争。山脊上携带无线电的海岸瞭望员预警来袭的空袭，侦察兵为巡逻队带路；军士长雅各布·武扎在遭受酷刑和刺刀伤后幸存，向陆战队通报了敌军的进攻。1943年2月，日本撤出约一万名幸存者，盟军在南太平洋转入攻势。

name.en: US nuclear tests in the Marshall Islands
name.zh: 美国在马绍尔群岛的核试验

summary.en: The United States moved the 167 people of Bikini Atoll in 1946 and carried out 67 nuclear tests at Bikini and Enewetak until 1958. The 1954 Castle Bravo hydrogen bomb, 1,000 times more powerful than Hiroshima, spread fallout on the inhabited atolls of Rongelap and Utirik and on a Japanese fishing boat. Bikini remains largely uninhabited.
summary.zh: 1946年，美国迁走比基尼环礁的167名居民，至1958年在比基尼和埃尼威托克共进行67次核试验。1954年的“喝彩城堡”氢弹威力是广岛原子弹的一千倍，放射性尘埃落在有人居住的朗格拉普、乌蒂里克环礁以及一艘日本渔船上。比基尼至今基本无人居住。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Bikini Atoll Nuclear Test Site
J. Weisgall, Operation Crossroads: The Atomic Tests at Bikini Atoll (Naval Institute Press, 1994)
Britannica: Bikini Atoll

story.en:
In February 1946 Commodore Ben Wyatt asked the Bikinians, after church, whether they would leave their atoll temporarily 'for the good of mankind and to end all world wars'. Their leader Juda is remembered as replying that they would go, and that everything was in God's hands. They were moved to Rongerik, where food ran short, and later to Kili.

That July, Operation Crossroads exploded two atomic bombs among a fleet of old warships at Bikini, watched by journalists from around the world. On 1 March 1954 the Castle Bravo test, a hydrogen bomb of 15 megatons, far exceeded its expected yield. Winds carried radioactive ash over Rongelap, where children played in what looked like snow; islanders suffered burns, hair loss and, later, thyroid cancers. The crew of the Japanese tuna boat Daigo Fukuryū Maru were also contaminated, and one man died.

Bikini was declared safe in the late 1960s and some families returned, only to be removed again in 1978 when their bodies showed high levels of radioactive caesium. The test site was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2010.
story.zh:
1946年2月，在一次礼拜之后，本·怀亚特准将问比基尼人能否“为了人类的福祉、为了终结一切世界大战”暂时离开他们的环礁。人们记得，他们的首领朱达回答说愿意离开，一切都在上帝手中。他们被迁往朗格里克，那里食物匮乏，后来又迁往基利岛。

同年7月，“十字路口行动”在比基尼的一支旧战舰编队中引爆了两颗原子弹，世界各地的记者到场观看。1954年3月1日，“喝彩城堡”试验的1500万吨级氢弹威力远超预期。风把放射性灰烬吹到朗格拉普，孩子们在看似雪花的落尘中玩耍；岛民遭受灼伤、脱发，后来又患上甲状腺癌。日本金枪鱼渔船“第五福龙丸”的船员也受到污染，一人死亡。

20世纪60年代末比基尼被宣布为安全，一些家庭迁回，却在1978年因体内放射性铯含量过高再次被迁走。2010年，该试验场被列入世界遗产名录。

name.zh: 英国在马拉林加的核试验

summary.en: Britain exploded seven atomic bombs at Maralinga in South Australia in 1956–57, after earlier tests at the Montebello Islands and Emu Field, and conducted hundreds of 'minor trials' that scattered plutonium until 1963. Anangu people were moved off their lands and some were exposed. A Royal Commission in 1984–85 exposed the failures.
summary.zh: 继蒙特贝洛群岛和埃米菲尔德的早期试验之后，英国于1956至1957年在南澳大利亚马拉林加引爆七颗原子弹，并在1963年前进行了数百次播撒钚的“小型试验”。阿南古人被迫离开故土，部分人受到辐射。1984至1985年的皇家调查委员会揭露了其中的种种失职。

sources.title: Royal Commission into British Nuclear Tests in Australia, Report (1985)
National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – Maralinga
ARPANSA: British nuclear weapons testing in Australia

story.en:
Prime Minister Robert Menzies agreed to Britain's request for a test range without consulting cabinet. After the first British bomb at the Montebello Islands in 1952, two tests at Emu Field in 1953 sent a black, oily cloud drifting over Wallatinna, where Yankunytjatjara people later described sickness and deaths; the British called it an unforeseen anomaly.

Maralinga, from a Garik word for thunder, was chosen as a permanent range on the lands of the Maralinga Tjarutja and other Anangu. Patrol officers were meant to keep people out of a vast area, but in 1957 the Milpuddie family was found camped in a bomb crater. Servicemen, many of them young national servicemen, were ordered to stand in the open as bombs exploded.

The 'minor trials' were worse in the long term, spreading about 22 kg of plutonium across the ground. The McClelland Royal Commission of 1984–85 condemned the tests' conduct; Britain contributed to a clean-up completed in 2000, and the last of the land was returned to the Maralinga Tjarutja in 2014.
story.zh:
总理罗伯特·孟席斯未经内阁讨论就同意了英国提出的试验场要求。1952年英国在蒙特贝洛群岛引爆第一颗原子弹后，1953年在埃米菲尔德的两次试验使一团黑色油腻的烟云飘过瓦拉蒂纳，扬昆察察拉人后来讲述了那里的病痛与死亡；英方称之为无法预料的异常现象。

马拉林加之名来自加里克语中的“雷”字，它被选为马拉林加·恰鲁恰人和其他阿南古人土地上的永久试验场。巡逻官本应把人们挡在大片区域之外，但1957年米尔普迪一家被发现在一个弹坑里扎营。许多年轻的服役士兵被命令在原子弹爆炸时站在空旷处。

从长远看，“小型试验”危害更大，约22公斤钚散落在地面上。1984至1985年的麦克莱兰皇家调查委员会谴责了试验的实施方式；英国出资参与了2000年完成的清理工作，2014年最后一批土地归还马拉林加·恰鲁恰人。

name.en: Hawaiʻi becomes the fiftieth US state
name.zh: 夏威夷成为美国第五十个州

summary.en: After decades of lobbying, Congress passed the Hawaii Admission Act in March 1959, and in a June plebiscite about 94 per cent of voters endorsed statehood; Hawaiʻi became the fiftieth state on 21 August. Native Hawaiian sovereignty advocates later argued that the ballot, which offered no choice of independence, could not legitimise the 1893 overthrow.
summary.zh: 经过数十年的游说，美国国会于1959年3月通过《夏威夷接纳法》，6月的全民投票中约94%的选民赞成建州；8月21日夏威夷成为美国第五十个州。夏威夷原住民主权倡导者后来指出，这次投票没有提供独立选项，不能使1893年的推翻行为合法化。

sources.title: Proclamation 3309: Admission of the State of Hawaii into the Union (21 August 1959), American Presidency Project
Britannica: Hawaii – Statehood
T. Coffman, The Island Edge of America: A Political History of Hawaiʻi (University of Hawaiʻi Press, 2003)

story.en:
Annexed in 1898, Hawaiʻi became a US territory in 1900, run by governors appointed in Washington and dominated economically by the 'Big Five' sugar and shipping firms. Its people, most of them of Asian descent by the 1920s, could not vote for president and had only a non-voting delegate in Congress. Statehood bills failed again and again, blocked by southern senators wary of a multiracial state and by fears of communist influence in the dockworkers' union.

The Second World War changed minds. After the attack on Pearl Harbor the islands spent three years under martial law, yet Japanese American soldiers of the 100th Infantry Battalion and the 442nd Regimental Combat Team became some of the most decorated in the US Army. In 1954 a new Democratic majority, many of them veterans, took control of the territorial legislature.

Congress passed the Admission Act in March 1959, and on 27 June islanders voted overwhelmingly for statehood. President Eisenhower proclaimed the fiftieth state on 21 August, and Daniel Inouye, a veteran of the 442nd, went to Washington as Hawaiʻi's first congressman. Native Hawaiian activists later argued that a vote offering only statehood or territorial status could not undo the overthrow of 1893.
story.zh:
夏威夷于1898年被吞并，1900年成为美国领地，由华盛顿任命的总督治理，经济上则由“五大公司”控制的制糖与航运业主导。到20世纪20年代，当地居民多数为亚裔，他们不能投票选举总统，在国会也只有一名无表决权的代表。建州议案屡屡失败，阻力来自担心出现一个多种族州的南方参议员，以及对码头工会受共产主义影响的忧虑。

第二次世界大战改变了人们的看法。珍珠港遇袭后，群岛实行了三年军事管制，而日裔美国人组成的第100步兵营和第442团级战斗队却成为美军中获勋最多的部队之一。1954年，以退伍军人为主的民主党新多数派掌控了领地议会。

1959年3月国会通过《接纳法》，6月27日岛民以压倒性多数赞成建州。8月21日艾森豪威尔总统宣布夏威夷成为第五十个州，第442团老兵丹尼尔·井上作为夏威夷首位众议员前往华盛顿。夏威夷原住民活动人士后来指出，一次只能在建州与维持领地之间选择的投票，无法抹去1893年的推翻。

name.zh: 西萨摩亚独立

summary.en: After a UN-supervised plebiscite in 1961, Western Samoa became the first Pacific Island territory to regain its independence, with Fiamē Mataʻafa Faumuina Mulinuʻu II as prime minister and the paramount chiefs Malietoa Tanumafili II and Tupua Tamasese Meaʻole as joint heads of state. A wave of Pacific independence followed.
summary.zh: 经1961年联合国监督的全民公决，西萨摩亚成为第一个重获独立的太平洋岛屿领地，由菲亚梅·马塔阿法·福穆伊纳·穆利努乌二世任总理，最高酋长马列托阿·塔努马菲利二世和图普阿·塔马塞塞·梅阿奥莱共任国家元首。此后太平洋掀起独立浪潮。

sources.title: NZHistory: Samoa independence
J. W. Davidson, Samoa mo Samoa: The Emergence of the Independent State of Western Samoa (Oxford University Press, 1967)

name.zh: 韦夫山罢工出走

summary.en: Vincent Lingiari led about 200 Gurindji stockmen, domestic workers and their families off the British-owned Wave Hill cattle station in protest at pay and conditions. The strike became a nine-year campaign for the return of their land; in 1975 Gough Whitlam poured soil into Lingiari's hand, a turning point toward the Aboriginal Land Rights Act of 1976.
summary.zh: 文森特·林吉亚里带领约200名古林吉族牧工、家佣及其家属离开英资韦夫山牧场，抗议工资和待遇。罢工演变为长达九年的土地归还运动；1975年高夫·惠特拉姆把泥土倒入林吉亚里手中，成为通向1976年《原住民土地权利法》的转折点。

sources.title: National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – Wave Hill walk-off
Australian Dictionary of Biography: Lingiari, Vincent
C. Wright & M. Hokari (eds), Gurindji Journey (Monash University, 2013)

story.en:
Aboriginal stockmen built the northern cattle industry, often for rations, tobacco and a fraction of white wages. In 1966 the Arbitration Commission granted equal pay but delayed it for three years. On 23 August, at Wave Hill station, run by the British Vestey company, Vincent Lingiari told the manager that his people were leaving, and they walked off to camp by the Victoria River.

What began as an industrial dispute became something larger. In 1967 the Gurindji moved to Wattie Creek, Daguragu, a place of significance in their Dreaming, and petitioned the governor-general for some 1,300 square kilometres of their country. Unionists, students and writers, among them Frank Hardy, raised money and publicity across Australia.

On 16 August 1975 Prime Minister Gough Whitlam came to Daguragu and handed over a lease, pouring a handful of red earth into Lingiari's palm, a moment captured by the photographer Mervyn Bishop. Lingiari replied that they were now all mates. The story became the song 'From Little Things Big Things Grow' by Paul Kelly and Kev Carmody.
story.zh:
北部畜牧业是由原住民牧工建立起来的，他们往往只得到口粮、烟草和白人工资的零头。1966年仲裁委员会裁定同工同酬，却推迟三年执行。8月23日，在英国维斯蒂公司经营的韦夫山牧场，文森特·林吉亚里告诉经理他的族人要离开了，他们徒步出走，在维多利亚河边扎营。

这场劳资纠纷演变成更宏大的运动。1967年，古林吉人迁往在他们“梦创”中意义重大的沃蒂溪（达古拉古），并向总督请愿，要求归还约1300平方公里的故土。工会成员、学生和弗兰克·哈迪等作家在全国募款并扩大影响。

1975年8月16日，总理高夫·惠特拉姆来到达古拉古移交租约，把一把红土倒入林吉亚里的掌心，摄影师默文·毕晓普记录下这一瞬间。林吉亚里回答说，如今大家都是朋友了。这段故事后来被保罗·凯利和凯夫·卡莫迪写成歌曲《星星之火终将燎原》。

name.en: French nuclear tests at Moruroa and Fangataufa
name.zh: 法国在穆鲁罗瓦和方阿陶法的核试验

summary.en: After leaving Algeria, France conducted 193 nuclear tests at Moruroa and Fangataufa atolls in French Polynesia, 46 of them atmospheric until 1974. Protests across the Pacific grew; the 1985 sinking of the Rainbow Warrior and the 1995–96 final series drew worldwide condemnation. France acknowledged health effects in 2010 and 2021.
summary.zh: 撤离阿尔及利亚后，法国在法属波利尼西亚的穆鲁罗瓦和方阿陶法环礁进行了193次核试验，其中46次为大气层试验，持续到1974年。太平洋各地的抗议日益高涨；1985年“彩虹勇士号”被炸沉以及1995至1996年最后一轮试验引起全世界谴责。法国于2010年和2021年承认了试验对健康的影响。

sources.title: Britannica: Mururoa Atoll
S. Philippe & T. Statius, Toxique: Enquête sur les essais nucléaires français en Polynésie (PUF, 2021)
CTBTO: French nuclear testing

note: The Wikidata item covers all French tests from 1960, including those in Algeria; this record covers the Pacific tests (1966–96).

name.zh: 1967年原住民问题公投

summary.en: Over 90 per cent of Australian voters approved removing two references to Aboriginal people from the Constitution, allowing them to be counted in the census and the Commonwealth to make laws for them. It did not grant citizenship or the vote, which most already had, but it became a powerful symbol of recognition.
summary.zh: 超过90%的澳大利亚选民赞成删除宪法中涉及原住民的两处条文，使他们得以计入人口普查，联邦也得以为其立法。公投并未授予公民身份或投票权（大多数原住民当时已有），但它成为承认原住民的有力象征。

sources.title: National Archives of Australia: The 1967 referendum
AIATSIS: The 1967 Referendum
B. Attwood & A. Markus, The 1967 Referendum: Race, Power and the Australian Constitution (AIATSIS, 2nd ed. 2007)

story.en:
The Constitution of 1901 said that 'aboriginal natives shall not be counted' in reckoning the population (section 127) and gave the Commonwealth power to make special laws for people of any race 'other than the aboriginal race in any State' (section 51(xxvi)). Through the 1950s and 1960s the Federal Council for the Advancement of Aborigines and Torres Strait Islanders, with campaigners such as Faith Bandler, Jessie Street and Kath Walker (Oodgeroo Noonuccal), gathered petitions to change this.

On 27 May 1967 Australians voted 90.77 per cent Yes, the largest majority in any Australian referendum, and every state agreed. Campaigners hoped that national power would end discriminatory state regimes over wages, movement and the removal of children.

The referendum is often misremembered as giving Aboriginal people citizenship or the right to vote; in fact Commonwealth voting rights had been extended in 1962. Its real effects came slowly, through land rights and other laws in the 1970s, but the vote showed that the nation wanted change.
story.zh:
1901年宪法第127条规定，统计人口时“原住民不计算在内”；第51条第26款则授权联邦为任何种族制定特别法律，但“各州的原住民种族除外”。整个20世纪50至60年代，原住民与托雷斯海峡岛民促进联合会以及费丝·班德勒、杰茜·斯特里特、凯丝·沃克（乌杰鲁·努纳卡尔）等活动家征集请愿，要求修改这些条文。

1967年5月27日，澳大利亚人以90.77%的赞成票通过，这是澳大利亚历次公投中最大的多数，所有州均表示赞成。运动人士希望，联邦权力能终结各州在工资、迁徙和带走儿童等方面的歧视性制度。

人们常误以为这次公投赋予了原住民公民身份或投票权；事实上联邦投票权早在1962年就已扩及原住民。它的实际作用来得缓慢，要靠20世纪70年代的土地权利法等法律体现，但这次投票表明整个国家渴望变革。

name.en: Mungo Lady and Mungo Man discovered
name.zh: 芒戈女士与芒戈男子的发现

summary.en: Geologist Jim Bowler found the cremated remains of a woman (1968) and the ochre-covered burial of a man (1974) in the dunes of dry Lake Mungo in New South Wales. Dated to about 40,000–42,000 years ago, they are the oldest known human remains in Australia and show some of the world's earliest ritual burial. Mungo Man was returned to Country in 2017.
summary.zh: 地质学家吉姆·鲍勒在新南威尔士州已干涸的芒戈湖沙丘中，先后发现一名女性的火葬遗骸（1968年）和一名男性涂有赭石的墓葬（1974年）。其年代约为四万至四万二千年前，是澳大利亚已知最古老的人类遗骸，也是世界上最早的仪式性埋葬之一。2017年芒戈男子回归故土。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Willandra Lakes Region
J. M. Bowler et al., 'New ages for human occupation and climatic change at Lake Mungo, Australia', Nature 421 (2003)
NSW National Parks: Mungo National Park

story.en:
Lake Mungo has been dry for some 15,000 years, but its crescent-shaped dune, the Walls of China, preserves layers from when it was full of water, fish and shellfish. In 1968 Jim Bowler noticed burnt bones eroding out of the sand. They belonged to a young woman who had been cremated, her bones broken and burned again, and buried in a small pit: the earliest known cremation anywhere.

In 1974, about 500 metres away, Bowler found a man laid on his back with his hands clasped and his body sprinkled with red ochre brought from far away. Optically stimulated luminescence dating in 2003 put both burials at around 40,000 years old.

The finds overturned the idea that people had reached Australia only recently and confirmed what Aboriginal people had always said about their deep connection to Country. The remains were taken to Canberra without the consent of the Paakantyi, Mutthi Mutthi and Ngiyampaa traditional owners. Mungo Lady was returned in 1992, and in November 2017 Mungo Man came home in a hearse that drove 800 km from Canberra, greeted by elders with a smoking ceremony.
story.zh:
芒戈湖干涸已有约一万五千年，但其新月形沙丘“中国长城”保存着湖中满是水、鱼和贝类时期的地层。1968年，吉姆·鲍勒注意到沙中露出被烧过的骨头。它们属于一位年轻女性：她被火化后，骨骼被打碎再焚烧，葬入一个小坑中，这是世界上已知最早的火葬。

1974年，在约500米外，鲍勒发现一名男子仰卧，双手交握，身上撒有从远方运来的红赭石。2003年的光释光测年把两处墓葬都定在约四万年前。

这些发现推翻了人类晚近才到达澳大利亚的观点，也证实了原住民一直以来所说的他们与故土的深远联系。遗骸当初未经帕坎提、穆提穆提和恩吉扬帕传统所有者同意就被运往堪培拉。芒戈女士于1992年归还；2017年11月，芒戈男子乘灵车从堪培拉行驶800公里回到故乡，长老们以烟熏仪式迎接。

name.en: Australian dishes relay the Apollo 11 moonwalk
name.zh: 澳大利亚天线转播阿波罗11号登月

summary.en: Because the Moon was above Australia when Neil Armstrong stepped out, NASA's Honeysuckle Creek station near Canberra and the 64-metre Parkes radio telescope in New South Wales received most of the television pictures seen by some 600 million people. Parkes carried the broadcast for over two hours despite gale-force winds.
summary.zh: 尼尔·阿姆斯特朗踏上月面时月球正位于澳大利亚上空，因此约六亿观众看到的电视画面大多由堪培拉附近的美国国家航空航天局蜜糖溪站和新南威尔士州64米口径的帕克斯射电望远镜接收。尽管狂风大作，帕克斯仍持续转播了两个多小时。

sources.title: CSIRO: Parkes and Apollo 11
J. Sarkissian, 'On Eagle's Wings: The Parkes Observatory's Support of the Apollo 11 Mission', Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia 18 (2001)

note: Honeysuckle Creek supplied the first minutes, including Armstrong's first step; Parkes took over for the rest of the moonwalk.

name.en: Papunya Tula and the Western Desert art movement
name.zh: 帕普尼亚图拉与西部沙漠艺术运动

summary.en: At Papunya, a government settlement west of Alice Springs, Pintupi, Luritja, Warlpiri and Anmatyerr men painted a Honey Ant Dreaming mural on the school wall with teacher Geoffrey Bardon, then transferred ceremonial designs to board and canvas. Their company, Papunya Tula Artists, founded in 1972, launched the dot-painting movement of world renown.
summary.zh: 在艾丽斯斯普林斯以西的政府定居点帕普尼亚，平图皮、卢里查、瓦尔皮里和安马蒂尔族男子与教师杰弗里·巴登一起在学校墙上绘制《蜜蚁梦创》壁画，随后把仪式图案移到木板和画布上。他们于1972年创立帕普尼亚图拉艺术家公司，开创了享誉世界的点画运动。

sources.title: Papunya Tula Artists: History
National Museum of Australia: Papunya Painting – Out of the Desert
G. Bardon & J. Bardon, Papunya: A Place Made After the Story (Miegunyah Press, 2004)

name.zh: 悉尼歌剧院落成

summary.en: Queen Elizabeth II opened the Sydney Opera House on Bennelong Point, designed by the Danish architect Jørn Utzon after he won a 1957 competition. Utzon resigned in 1966 amid disputes over cost and design and never saw it finished. It was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2007.
summary.zh: 伊丽莎白二世为本尼朗角上的悉尼歌剧院揭幕。歌剧院由丹麦建筑师约恩·乌松设计，他在1957年的竞赛中胜出。1966年乌松因造价和设计纠纷辞职，生前从未见到它竣工。2007年歌剧院列入世界遗产名录。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Sydney Opera House
P. Murray, The Saga of Sydney Opera House (Spon Press, 2004)

name.zh: 热带气旋“崔西”摧毁达尔文

summary.en: In the early hours of Christmas Day a small but intense cyclone passed over Darwin, killing 71 people (49 on land, 22 at sea) and destroying or badly damaging about 70 per cent of the city's homes. More than 35,000 of its roughly 47,000 residents were evacuated, most of them by air.
summary.zh: 圣诞节凌晨，一个范围不大但极为强烈的热带气旋掠过达尔文，造成71人死亡（陆上49人，海上22人），全市约七成住宅被毁或严重受损。约4.7万居民中有3.5万多人被疏散，其中大多数经空运撤离。

sources.title: National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – Cyclone Tracy
National Archives of Australia: Cyclone Tracy, Darwin (fact sheet 176)
Bureau of Meteorology: Tropical Cyclone Tracy

note: Early counts gave 65–66 deaths; the 2005 coroner's figure of 71 includes those lost at sea.

story.en:
Tracy formed in the Arafura Sea on 21 December 1974 and at first seemed set to pass Darwin by. On Christmas Eve it turned toward the city, and many residents, busy with celebrations and used to false alarms, paid little heed to the warnings. Soon after midnight winds of well over 200 km/h began tearing apart the elevated timber-and-fibro houses typical of the north; the airport anemometer failed after recording a gust of 217 km/h.

By dawn whole suburbs were flattened, power, water and sewerage had failed, and the town was cut off. Major-General Alan Stretton of the Natural Disasters Organisation flew in to take charge. Within about a week more than 35,000 people, most of them women and children, had been flown or driven out, while those who stayed cleared debris and buried the dead.

Darwin was rebuilt under a reconstruction commission, with new building codes requiring houses to be tied down against cyclonic winds, standards later adopted across northern Australia. Tracy remains the benchmark for disaster response in Australia and is remembered in Darwin every Christmas.
story.zh:
“崔西”于1974年12月21日在阿拉弗拉海形成，起初似乎会从达尔文旁边掠过。平安夜它转向城市，许多居民忙于过节，又习惯了虚惊，没有把警报放在心上。午夜过后不久，时速远超200公里的狂风开始撕裂北部常见的架高式木板和纤维水泥房屋；机场风速计在记录到每小时217公里的阵风后失灵。

天亮时，整片整片的城区被夷平，电力、供水和排污系统瘫痪，城市与外界隔绝。国家灾害组织的艾伦·斯特雷顿少将飞抵现场主持救灾。大约一周之内，3.5万多人（大多是妇女和儿童）经空运或陆路撤离，留下的人清理废墟、掩埋死者。

达尔文在重建委员会主持下重建，新的建筑规范要求房屋牢固锚定以抵御气旋强风，这些标准后来推广到整个澳大利亚北部。“崔西”至今仍是澳大利亚灾害应对的标杆，每逢圣诞节达尔文都会纪念它。

name.zh: 巴布亚新几内亚独立

summary.en: Australia's territories of Papua and New Guinea, unified in administration since 1949, became the independent state of Papua New Guinea, with Michael Somare as prime minister. The Australian flag was lowered at Port Moresby's Sir Hubert Murray Stadium the evening before. Bougainville's secessionists had declared their own republic two weeks earlier.
summary.zh: 自1949年起合并管理的澳大利亚属巴布亚和新几内亚两领地成为独立的巴布亚新几内亚国，由迈克尔·索马雷任总理。前一天傍晚，澳大利亚国旗在莫尔兹比港休伯特·默里爵士体育场降下。两周前，布干维尔分离主义者已宣布成立自己的共和国。

sources.title: Britannica: Papua New Guinea – Independence
Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade: Australia and PNG independence documents
D. Denoon, A Trial Separation: Australia and the Decolonisation of Papua New Guinea (ANU Press, 2012)

story.en:
Until the 1960s many Australian officials assumed independence for New Guinea was generations away. The highlands had first been explored by outsiders only in the 1930s, and there were few university graduates. United Nations criticism, a new generation of leaders and the election of Gough Whitlam's government in 1972 sped things up dramatically.

Michael Somare, a former teacher and radio broadcaster from the Sepik, had co-founded the Pangu Party in 1967. He became chief minister in 1972, led the territory to self-government in December 1973, and steered a constitution written by Papua New Guineans for a country of some 800 languages and thousands of clans.

Independence came peacefully on 16 September 1975. Prince Charles represented the Queen, who remained head of state. Tensions over land and mining royalties on Bougainville, where the giant Panguna copper mine had opened in 1972, foreshadowed the conflict that would erupt there in 1988.
story.zh:
直到20世纪60年代，许多澳大利亚官员仍认为新几内亚独立还要等上几代人。外人直到20世纪30年代才首次深入高原，大学毕业生寥寥无几。联合国的批评、新一代领导人的崛起以及1972年高夫·惠特拉姆政府的上台，使进程大大加快。

来自塞皮克的前教师和电台广播员迈克尔·索马雷于1967年参与创建潘古党。他于1972年出任首席部长，1973年12月带领领地实现自治，并主持制定了一部由巴新人自己撰写的宪法，适用于一个拥有约800种语言和数千个氏族的国家。

1975年9月16日，独立和平到来。查尔斯王子代表仍为国家元首的女王出席。布干维尔巨大的潘古纳铜矿于1972年投产，围绕土地和采矿收益的紧张关系预示了1988年将在那里爆发的冲突。

name.en: Māori land march (Te Rōpū o te Matakite)
name.zh: 毛利土地大游行

summary.en: Led by 79-year-old Whina Cooper, marchers walked about 1,100 km from Te Hāpua in the far north to Parliament in Wellington between 14 September and 13 October 1975, under the slogan 'Not one more acre of Māori land'. About 5,000 arrived and presented a petition with 60,000 signatures. The Waitangi Tribunal was created the same year.
summary.zh: 在79岁的菲娜·库珀带领下，游行者于1975年9月14日至10月13日从最北端的特哈普阿步行约1100公里到惠灵顿的议会，口号是“毛利人的土地一英亩也不再让”。约5000人抵达，递交了有6万人签名的请愿书。同年设立了怀唐伊特别法庭。

sources.title: NZHistory: Māori land march
Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: Ngā rōpū whakahaere – Māori protest

name.zh: “霍库莱阿号”航行至塔希提

summary.en: The double-hulled voyaging canoe Hōkūleʻa, built by the Polynesian Voyaging Society, sailed some 4,400 km from Maui to Tahiti in 34 days, navigated without instruments by Mau Piailug of Satawal. Some 17,000 people greeted its arrival at Papeʻete. The voyage disproved claims that Polynesians had settled the Pacific by accidental drift.
summary.zh: 由波利尼西亚航海协会建造的双体航海独木舟“霍库莱阿号”在萨塔瓦尔岛的毛·皮艾卢格不借助任何仪器的导航下，用34天从毛伊岛航行约4400公里抵达塔希提。约1.7万人在帕皮提迎接。这次航行驳斥了波利尼西亚人是偶然漂流而定居太平洋的说法。

label.zh: 土阿莫土群岛马泰瓦：初见陆地

sources.title: Polynesian Voyaging Society: Hōkūleʻa history
B. Finney, Hokuleʻa: The Way to Tahiti (Dodd, Mead, 1979)
B. Finney, Voyage of Rediscovery (University of California Press, 1994)

story.en:
In the 1950s the writer Andrew Sharp argued that Polynesians could not have navigated deliberately across thousands of kilometres, and must have reached their islands by lucky drift. The anthropologist Ben Finney, the artist Herb Kawainui Kāne and the waterman Tommy Holmes founded the Polynesian Voyaging Society in 1973 to test the question at sea. Their canoe, Hōkūleʻa, 'Star of Gladness', was launched in 1975.

No Hawaiian still knew the old wayfinding, so they turned to Mau Piailug, a master navigator from Satawal in Micronesia. Leaving Maui on 1 May 1976, he steered by the rising and setting points of stars, the direction of the swells, and the sun; when clouds hid the sky he lay in the hull to feel the waves. Tensions among the crew boiled over at times, but after a month seabirds and a change in the swells told Mau land was near, and on 1 June they made landfall at Mataiva.

At Papeʻete on 4 June, about 17,000 people, more than half the town, came out to greet them. The voyage sparked the Hawaiian Renaissance, and Mau went on to teach Nainoa Thompson, who later navigated Hōkūleʻa around the world.
story.zh:
20世纪50年代，作家安德鲁·夏普认为波利尼西亚人不可能有意识地跨越数千公里航行，他们一定是靠幸运的漂流到达各岛的。为了在海上检验这一问题，人类学家本·芬尼、画家赫伯·卡瓦伊努伊·卡内和水手汤米·霍姆斯于1973年创立波利尼西亚航海协会。他们的独木舟“霍库莱阿号”意为“欢乐之星”，于1975年下水。

夏威夷已无人通晓古老的导航术，于是他们求助于密克罗尼西亚萨塔瓦尔岛的航海大师毛·皮艾卢格。1976年5月1日离开毛伊岛后，他依据星辰升落的方位、涌浪的方向和太阳掌舵；云层遮蔽天空时，他就躺在船体中感受波浪。船员之间不时爆发矛盾，但一个月后，海鸟和涌浪的变化告诉毛陆地已近，6月1日他们抵达马泰瓦岛。

6月4日在帕皮提，约1.7万人（超过全城人口的一半）出来迎接。这次航行点燃了“夏威夷文化复兴”，毛后来又教授奈诺阿·汤普森，后者日后驾驶“霍库莱阿号”完成了环球航行。

name.zh: 瓦努阿图独立

summary.en: The New Hebrides, ruled since 1906 by a unique Anglo-French Condominium, became independent as the Republic of Vanuatu, with the Anglican priest Walter Lini as prime minister. A secessionist revolt on Espiritu Santo led by Jimmy Stevens's Nagriamel movement was ended weeks later by Papua New Guinean troops.
summary.zh: 自1906年起由独特的英法共管政府统治的新赫布里底群岛独立为瓦努阿图共和国，由圣公会牧师沃尔特·利尼任总理。吉米·史蒂文斯领导的纳格里亚梅尔运动在圣埃斯皮里图岛发动分离叛乱，数周后被巴布亚新几内亚军队平息。

sources.title: Britannica: Vanuatu – History
H. Van Trease, The Politics of Land in Vanuatu: From Colony to Independence (Institute of Pacific Studies, USP, 1987)
RNZ: Vanuatu – a brief history

note: Wikidata has no item for the independence event itself; the Santo revolt is Q3446722 (Coconut War).

story.en:
For three-quarters of a century the New Hebrides had two of almost everything: two police forces, two school systems, two currencies and two prisons, plus a Joint Court whose president was for decades appointed by the king of Spain. Under the Anglo-French Condominium formalised in 1906, ni-Vanuatu were subjects of neither power and citizens of no state.

From the late 1960s anger at the alienation of land to foreign planters fed the Nagriamel movement on Espiritu Santo and then the New Hebrides National Party, later the Vanuaʻaku Pati, led by Father Walter Lini. Britain was ready to leave; France, mindful of New Caledonia, hesitated, and French-speaking and plantation interests favoured autonomy for Santo and Tanna.

In May 1980 Jimmy Stevens and his followers, encouraged by some French settlers and an American libertarian group, seized Luganville and proclaimed a 'Republic of Vemerana'. Independence went ahead on 30 July. Lini then asked Papua New Guinea for help, and PNG troops, flown in by Australia, ended the so-called Coconut War within weeks; Stevens surrendered at the start of September. The new constitution returned all land to its custom owners, reversing a century of alienation.
story.zh:
在四分之三个世纪里，新赫布里底群岛几乎什么都是双份：两支警察、两套学校体系、两种货币、两座监狱，还有一个院长几十年间由西班牙国王任命的联合法院。在1906年正式确立的英法共管体制下，当地的尼瓦努阿图人既非英国臣民也非法国臣民，不属于任何国家。

20世纪60年代末起，对土地被外国种植园主占有的愤怒催生了圣埃斯皮里图岛上的纳格里亚梅尔运动，继而催生了新赫布里底国民党，即后来由沃尔特·利尼神父领导的瓦努阿库党。英国愿意撤离；法国顾及新喀里多尼亚而犹豫不决，讲法语的群体和种植园利益集团则支持圣埃斯皮里图岛和塔纳岛自治。

1980年5月，吉米·史蒂文斯及其追随者在部分法国移民和一个美国自由意志主义团体的怂恿下占领卢甘维尔，宣布成立“韦梅拉纳共和国”。7月30日独立如期举行。随后利尼请求巴布亚新几内亚援助，由澳大利亚空运抵达的巴新军队在数周内结束了所谓的“椰子战争”；史蒂文斯于9月初投降。新宪法把全部土地归还给习惯法所有者，扭转了一个世纪以来的土地流失。

name.zh: “彩虹勇士号”被炸沉

summary.en: French secret service agents sank Greenpeace's flagship Rainbow Warrior with two bombs in Auckland harbour as it prepared to lead a protest flotilla to Moruroa, killing the photographer Fernando Pereira. Two agents were caught and convicted. The attack strengthened New Zealand's nuclear-free policy, enacted into law in 1987.
summary.zh: 法国情报机构特工在奥克兰港用两枚炸弹炸沉绿色和平组织的旗舰“彩虹勇士号”，当时该船正准备率领抗议船队前往穆鲁罗瓦，摄影师费尔南多·佩雷拉遇难。两名特工被抓获定罪。这次袭击强化了新西兰的无核政策，该政策于1987年写入法律。

sources.title: NZHistory: Sinking of the Rainbow Warrior
Britannica: Rainbow Warrior

name.zh: 1987年斐济政变

summary.en: A month after Timoci Bavadra's Labour-led coalition, backed mainly by Indo-Fijians, took office, Lieutenant-Colonel Sitiveni Rabuka seized Parliament in Suva, the first military coup in the South Pacific. A second coup in September led to a republic and a constitution favouring indigenous Fijians; many Indo-Fijians emigrated.
summary.zh: 以印度裔斐济人为主要支持者的蒂莫西·巴瓦德拉工党联合政府上台一个月后，西蒂维尼·兰布卡中校在苏瓦占领议会，这是南太平洋第一次军事政变。9月的第二次政变导致成立共和国并制定偏向原住民斐济人的宪法；许多印度裔斐济人移居海外。

sources.title: B. V. Lal, Power and Prejudice: The Making of the Fiji Crisis (NZ Institute of International Affairs, 1988)
Britannica: Fiji – The 1987 coups

name.zh: 布干维尔冲突与独立公投

summary.en: Anger over environmental damage and revenues from the Panguna copper mine led landowners under Francis Ona to sabotage it in 1988, starting a war between the Bougainville Revolutionary Army and PNG forces that killed perhaps 15,000–20,000 people. A 2001 peace agreement promised a referendum; in 2019 97.7 per cent voted for independence.
summary.zh: 因潘古纳铜矿造成的环境破坏和收益分配问题，弗朗西斯·奥纳领导的土地所有者于1988年破坏矿山，引发布干维尔革命军与巴新部队之间的战争，约1.5万至2万人死亡。2001年和平协议承诺举行公投；2019年97.7%的选民赞成独立。

sources.title: A. J. Regan, Light Intervention: Lessons from Bougainville (US Institute of Peace, 2010)
Britannica: Bougainville

note: Death toll estimates vary widely; the result of the non-binding 2019 referendum still awaits ratification by PNG's parliament.

name.zh: 马宝案判决推翻“无主地”原则

summary.en: In Mabo v Queensland (No 2) the High Court of Australia ruled 6–1 that the Meriam people held native title to their lands on Mer in the Torres Strait, rejecting the doctrine that Australia had been terra nullius, land belonging to no one, when Britain claimed it. The Native Title Act 1993 followed.
summary.zh: 在“马宝诉昆士兰州（第2号）案”中，澳大利亚高等法院以6比1裁定，托雷斯海峡梅尔岛上的梅里亚姆人对其土地享有原住民产权，否定了英国宣称主权时澳大利亚是“无主地”的学说。随后出台了1993年《原住民产权法》。

sources.title: High Court of Australia, Mabo v Queensland (No 2) [1992] HCA 23
National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – Mabo decision
AIATSIS: The Mabo case

story.en:
Eddie Koiki Mabo grew up on Mer, where his family's garden plots had been passed down for generations under Meriam law. Working at James Cook University in Townsville in the 1970s, he talked with the historians Henry Reynolds and Noel Loos, who told him that in Australian law his land belonged to the Crown. He was stunned.

In 1982 Mabo and four other Meriam people, among them David Passi and James Rice, sued Queensland. The Queensland government tried to extinguish their claim with a retrospective law in 1985, but the High Court struck it down in 1988 as racially discriminatory. Years of hearings followed, in which Mabo's own testimony about his family's land was attacked as hearsay. He died of cancer in January 1992.

On 3 June 1992 the High Court ruled that the common law of Australia recognised a form of native title where Indigenous people had kept their connection to the land and where it had not been extinguished by a valid grant. Justices Deane and Gaudron called the dispossession a 'legacy of unutterable shame'. Mabo was reburied on Mer in 1995, and 3 June is now Mabo Day.
story.zh:
埃迪·柯伊基·马宝在梅尔岛长大，他家的园圃依梅里亚姆律法世代相传。20世纪70年代在汤斯维尔的詹姆斯·库克大学工作时，他与历史学家亨利·雷诺兹和诺埃尔·卢斯交谈，得知在澳大利亚法律中他的土地属于王室。他大为震惊。

1982年，马宝与戴维·帕西、詹姆斯·赖斯等另外四名梅里亚姆人起诉昆士兰州。昆士兰政府在1985年试图以溯及既往的法律消灭他们的诉求，但高等法院于1988年以种族歧视为由将其推翻。此后多年的庭审中，马宝关于自家土地的证词被指为传闻证据而遭攻击。1992年1月，他因癌症去世。

1992年6月3日，高等法院裁定：凡原住民保持着与土地的联系、且未被有效授地消灭之处，澳大利亚普通法承认某种形式的原住民产权。迪恩和高德伦两位大法官称这种剥夺是“难以言说的耻辱遗产”。1995年马宝重葬于梅尔岛，6月3日如今被定为“马宝日”。

name.en: Nouméa Accord and New Caledonia's independence referendums
name.zh: 《努美阿协议》与新喀里多尼亚独立公投

summary.en: Ten years after the Matignon Accords ended the violent 'Events' of the 1980s, France, the pro-independence FLNKS and the loyalist RPCR agreed to transfer powers gradually to New Caledonia, recognise Kanak identity and the wrongs of colonisation, and hold up to three independence referendums. Voters chose France in 2018 and 2020; independence supporters boycotted the 2021 vote.
summary.zh: 《马提尼翁协议》结束20世纪80年代的暴力“事件”十年后，法国、主张独立的卡纳克社会主义民族解放阵线和忠于法国的保卫喀里多尼亚共和联盟达成协议：逐步向新喀里多尼亚移交权力，承认卡纳克人的身份与殖民时代的过错，并举行至多三次独立公投。2018年和2020年选民选择留在法国，2021年的公投遭独立派抵制。

sources.title: Accord sur la Nouvelle-Calédonie signé à Nouméa le 5 mai 1998 (Journal officiel de la République française, 27 May 1998)
Britannica: New Caledonia – History
D. Chappell, 'A Decolonisation Test for France in the Pacific', ANU Department of Pacific Affairs In Brief 2022/15

note: The FLNKS does not recognise the 2021 result; New Caledonia's future status was still under negotiation in 2025.

story.en:
In the 1980s New Caledonia came close to civil war. Kanak independence activists of the FLNKS, led by Jean-Marie Tjibaou, boycotted elections and blocked roads, while loyalists, many descended from settlers and convicts, insisted on staying French. In April 1988 militants on Ouvéa killed four gendarmes and held others hostage in a cave; the French assault in May left nineteen Kanak and two soldiers dead.

Shaken, both camps signed the Matignon Accords that June, promising development for Kanak areas and a vote in ten years. Tjibaou was assassinated in 1989 by a Kanak opponent of the compromise. In 1998, rather than risk an all-or-nothing vote, Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, the FLNKS and Jacques Lafleur's RPCR signed a new accord at Nouméa. Its preamble acknowledged the injustices of colonisation; it created a New Caledonian citizenship, restricted the electoral roll for provincial elections and transferred powers step by step.

The referendums came in 2018 (56.7 per cent No), 2020 (53.3 per cent No) and December 2021, when the independence camp boycotted a vote held during a COVID outbreak and 96.5 per cent voted No. A plan to unfreeze the electoral roll set off deadly riots in May 2024, and the islands' future status is still being negotiated.
story.zh:
20世纪80年代，新喀里多尼亚一度濒临内战。让-玛丽·吉巴乌领导的卡纳克社会主义民族解放阵线独立派抵制选举、封锁道路，而许多身为移民和流放犯后代的忠诚派则坚持留在法国。1988年4月，武装分子在乌韦阿岛杀死四名宪兵，并把其他人扣作人质藏在山洞中；5月法军强攻，造成19名卡纳克人和2名士兵死亡。

震惊之下，双方于当年6月签署《马提尼翁协议》，承诺发展卡纳克人地区，并在十年后举行公投。1989年吉巴乌被一名反对妥协的卡纳克人刺杀。1998年，为避免一次定输赢的公投，法国总理利昂内尔·若斯潘、民族解放阵线和雅克·拉夫勒尔领导的保卫喀里多尼亚共和联盟在努美阿签署新协议。协议序言承认殖民时代的不公，设立新喀里多尼亚公民身份，限制省级选举的选民名册，并分阶段移交权力。

公投分别于2018年（56.7%反对独立）、2020年（53.3%反对）和2021年12月举行；最后一次因正值新冠疫情暴发而遭独立派抵制，96.5%的投票者反对独立。2024年5月，一项放开选民名册的计划引发致命骚乱，群岛未来的地位至今仍在谈判之中。

name.en: National Apology to the Stolen Generations
name.zh: 向“被偷走的一代”的国家道歉

summary.en: Prime Minister Kevin Rudd moved a motion in Parliament apologising to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, especially the Stolen Generations, children removed from their families under government policies from about 1910 to the 1970s. The Bringing Them Home report of 1997 had estimated that between one in three and one in ten Indigenous children were taken.
summary.zh: 总理陆克文在议会提出动议，向原住民和托雷斯海峡岛民，特别是“被偷走的一代”道歉。他们是约1910年至20世纪70年代间依政府政策被带离家庭的儿童。1997年《带他们回家》报告估计，每三到十名原住民儿童中就有一人被带走。

sources.title: Parliament of Australia: Apology to Australia's Indigenous Peoples (13 February 2008)
Australian Human Rights Commission: Bringing Them Home report (1997)
National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – The Apology

story.en:
For much of the 20th century, state and federal 'protection' and assimilation laws let officials remove Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children, especially those of mixed descent, to missions, institutions and white foster homes. Many were told their parents were dead or did not want them; many were abused. In 1997 the inquiry led by Sir Ronald Wilson and Mick Dodson published Bringing Them Home, built on the testimony of 535 people.

The Howard government expressed regret but refused a formal apology. Kevin Rudd promised one during the 2007 election. On the morning of 13 February 2008 thousands gathered on the lawns of Parliament House and in public squares across the country to watch on giant screens, and Stolen Generations members sat in the chamber.

Rudd said sorry three times: to the mothers and fathers, the brothers and sisters, and to the families and communities torn apart. The Opposition supported the motion. In Federation Square in Melbourne and on the lawns in Canberra, people wept and some turned their backs at points of the Opposition leader's speech. The apology was followed by targets to 'Close the Gap' in health, education and life expectancy.
story.zh:
在20世纪的大部分时间里，州和联邦的“保护”与同化法律允许官员把原住民和托雷斯海峡岛民儿童，尤其是混血儿童，带到传教站、收容机构和白人寄养家庭。许多孩子被告知父母已死或不要他们，许多人遭受虐待。1997年，由罗纳德·威尔逊爵士和米克·多德森主持的调查发表了《带他们回家》报告，依据的是535人的证词。

霍华德政府表示遗憾，但拒绝正式道歉。陆克文在2007年大选中承诺道歉。2008年2月13日上午，数千人聚集在议会大厦草坪和全国各地的广场上，通过大屏幕观看，“被偷走的一代”成员则坐在议事厅中。

陆克文三次说“对不起”：向母亲和父亲，向兄弟和姐妹，向被拆散的家庭与社群。反对党支持这项动议。在墨尔本联邦广场和堪培拉的草坪上，人们落泪，也有人在反对党领袖发言的某些段落时转过身去。道歉之后，政府设定了在健康、教育和预期寿命方面“缩小差距”的目标。

name.en: Uluru Statement from the Heart and the Voice referendum
name.zh: 《乌卢鲁心声宣言》与“发声”公投

summary.en: About 250 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander delegates meeting near Uluru called for 'Voice, Treaty, Truth': a constitutionally enshrined Indigenous Voice to Parliament, then a process of agreement-making and truth-telling. In the referendum of 14 October 2023, the Voice proposal was rejected nationally, with about 60 per cent voting No.
summary.zh: 约250名原住民和托雷斯海峡岛民代表在乌卢鲁附近集会，呼吁“发声、条约、真相”：在宪法中设立原住民向议会发声的机构，进而启动协议缔结与真相陈述进程。在2023年10月14日的公投中，“发声”提案在全国被否决，约60%的选民投了反对票。

sources.title: Uluru Statement from the Heart
Australian Electoral Commission: 2023 referendum results

name.zh: 洪阿汤加—洪阿哈阿帕伊火山喷发

summary.en: The submarine volcano 65 km north of Nukuʻalofa produced the largest explosion recorded by modern instruments, with a plume reaching about 57 km into the mesosphere and a pressure wave that circled the earth several times. Tsunamis struck Tonga and crossed the Pacific, ash covered Tongatapu and the undersea internet cable was severed.
summary.zh: 位于努库阿洛法以北65公里的海底火山发生现代仪器记录以来最大的爆炸，烟柱升至约57公里高的中间层，冲击波绕地球数周。海啸袭击汤加并横越太平洋，火山灰覆盖汤加塔布岛，海底互联网电缆被切断。

sources.title: NASA Earth Observatory: Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai erupts
S. Proud et al., 'The January 2022 eruption of Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai volcano reached the mesosphere', Science 378 (2022)

story.en:
The volcano had built a small new island between the islets of Hunga Tonga and Hunga Haʻapai in 2015. In December 2021 it began erupting, and on the evening of 15 January 2022 it exploded, sending out an atmospheric pressure wave comparable to that of Krakatoa in 1883. Satellites showed an umbrella cloud 500 km wide; its top reached about 57 km, the highest volcanic plume ever measured.

The atmospheric shock wave was recorded by barometers worldwide and circled the planet repeatedly; people heard booms in Alaska. Tsunami waves up to 15 metres high swept the western coast of Tongatapu and small islands like Mango and Fonoifua, whose villages were destroyed. Because the only fibre-optic cable was cut, Tonga was cut off from the world for days, and its diaspora waited anxiously for news.

Only about six people died, among them two drowned by the tsunami in Peru, a remarkably low toll that Tongans credit partly to warnings and quick evacuation. The eruption also injected an unprecedented amount of water vapour into the stratosphere.
story.zh:
这座火山在2015年于洪阿汤加和洪阿哈阿帕伊两座小岛之间形成了一座新小岛。2021年12月它开始喷发，2022年1月15日傍晚发生大爆炸，其产生的大气压力波可与1883年喀拉喀托火山爆发相比。卫星图像显示伞状云宽达500公里，顶部高约57公里，是有史以来测得的最高火山烟柱。

大气冲击波被世界各地的气压计记录下来，并反复环绕地球；阿拉斯加的人们都听到了轰鸣。高达15米的海啸席卷汤加塔布岛西海岸以及芒戈、福诺伊富阿等小岛，村庄被毁。由于唯一的光缆被切断，汤加与外界失联多日，海外侨民焦急地等待消息。

死亡人数仅约六人，其中两人在秘鲁被海啸淹死。汤加人认为如此低的死亡人数部分要归功于预警和迅速疏散。这次喷发还向平流层注入了前所未有的大量水汽。

name.zh: 拉海纳山火

summary.en: Driven by hurricane-force winds and dry non-native grasses, a wildfire swept through Lahaina on Maui, killing 102 people and destroying more than 2,200 buildings, including much of the historic former royal capital. It was the deadliest US wildfire in over a century.
summary.zh: 在飓风级强风和干燥的外来草种推动下，一场山火席卷毛伊岛拉海纳，造成102人死亡，2200多座建筑被毁，昔日王都的历史街区大部分化为灰烬。这是美国一个多世纪以来最致命的山火。

sources.title: Maui Police Department / County of Maui: Maui wildfires updates
Britannica: 2023 Hawaii wildfires

name.en: Murujuga rock art inscribed as World Heritage
name.zh: 穆鲁朱加岩画列入世界遗产

summary.en: UNESCO inscribed the Murujuga Cultural Landscape on the Burrup Peninsula and Dampier Archipelago, home to perhaps a million petroglyphs, some thought to be among the oldest in the world, on the World Heritage List after a campaign by its Ngarda-Ngarli traditional owners. Industrial emissions nearby remain a concern.
summary.zh: 在恩加尔达-恩加尔利传统所有者的推动下，联合国教科文组织把位于伯鲁普半岛和丹皮尔群岛的穆鲁朱加文化景观列入世界遗产名录。这里或有上百万幅岩刻，其中一些被认为是世界上最古老的岩画之一。附近工业排放的影响仍令人担忧。

sources.title: Murujuga Aboriginal Corporation: World Heritage listing
University of Western Australia: We were part of the World Heritage listing of Murujuga (July 2025)
National Indigenous Times: UNESCO includes Murujuga Cultural Landscape on World Heritage List (11 July 2025)

note: Ages of the oldest engravings are estimated from weathering and sea-level history (perhaps up to 40,000–50,000 years); direct dating is difficult.

story.en:
Murujuga, on the Pilbara coast of Western Australia, is a landscape of red-brown boulders whose dark weathered surfaces have been pecked and scratched for tens of thousands of years. The engravings show human figures, emu tracks, turtles, kangaroos and the thylacine (Tasmanian tiger), which disappeared from the mainland thousands of years ago. Some motifs depict animals of the land that was drowned when sea levels rose after the last Ice Age.

For the Ngarda-Ngarli, the five language groups with responsibility for Murujuga, the engravings are not relics but part of living law, linked to songlines that cross the country. They are an archive of how people experienced a changing coast over a timescale that makes the atlas's two thousand years seem brief.

Since the 1960s the peninsula has also hosted ports, an iron-ore and gas industry and fertiliser plants; part of the rock art was moved or destroyed. The traditional owners campaigned for more than twenty years for protection. On 11 July 2025 the World Heritage Committee, meeting in Paris, inscribed the Murujuga Cultural Landscape, the second Australian site listed solely for Aboriginal cultural values after Budj Bim.
story.zh:
穆鲁朱加位于西澳大利亚皮尔巴拉海岸，遍布红褐色巨石，其风化变暗的表面数万年来被人们凿刻和划刻。岩刻描绘了人像、鸸鹋足迹、海龟、袋鼠，以及数千年前就已从大陆消失的袋狼。有些图案描绘的是末次冰期后海平面上升时被淹没的土地上的动物。

对于肩负守护穆鲁朱加之责的五个语言群体，即恩加尔达-恩加尔利人来说，这些岩刻不是遗物，而是活着的律法的一部分，与穿越大地的歌之路相连。它们记录了人们如何经历不断变化的海岸，其时间跨度使本地图集的两千年显得短暂。

自20世纪60年代起，这一半岛还建起了港口、铁矿石和天然气产业以及化肥厂，部分岩画被迁移或毁坏。传统所有者为保护它奔走了二十多年。2025年7月11日，在巴黎召开的世界遗产委员会会议把穆鲁朱加文化景观列入名录，这是继巴奇必姆之后，澳大利亚第二处仅因原住民文化价值而入选的遗产。

name.zh: 珍珠港事件

summary.en: On the morning of 7 December 1941, aircraft from six Japanese carriers under Vice Admiral Chūichi Nagumo struck the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor on Oʻahu. In two waves they sank or damaged all eight battleships and destroyed 188 aircraft, killing about 2,400 Americans. The United States declared war on Japan the next day.
summary.zh: 1941年12月7日清晨，南云忠一中将指挥的六艘日本航空母舰派出飞机，袭击停泊在瓦胡岛珍珠港的美国太平洋舰队。两波攻击击沉或击伤全部八艘战列舰，摧毁188架飞机，约2400名美国人丧生。次日美国对日宣战。

sources.title: National Park Service, Pearl Harbor National Memorial: People (casualty figures)
Naval History and Heritage Command: USS Arizona (BB-39)
Wikipedia: Attack on Pearl Harbor

note: Death tolls differ slightly: the National Park Service counts 2,390 (2,341 service members and 49 civilians); other tallies give 2,403 including 68 civilians.

story.en:
Japan's leaders planned the raid to stop the US Pacific Fleet from interfering with their advance into Southeast Asia. Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto, commander of the Combined Fleet, pressed for it, and a striking force of six carriers under Vice Admiral Chūichi Nagumo launched 353 aircraft in two waves.

The first wave arrived at 7:48 a.m. on a Sunday. A bomb set off the forward magazine of the battleship Arizona, killing 1,177 of the 1,512 men aboard, the heaviest loss of any ship; 429 more died when the Oklahoma capsized. The National Park Service counts 2,390 Americans killed, 49 of them civilians. Japan lost 29 aircraft, five midget submarines and about 130 men, and Ensign Kazuo Sakamaki, from one of the submarines, became the first Japanese prisoner of the war.

The attack missed what mattered most. The fleet's three carriers were at sea, and the oil tanks, repair yards and submarine base were left untouched. Calling 7 December "a date which will live in infamy", President Roosevelt took the United States into the Second World War on 8 December.
story.zh:
日本领导层策划这次袭击，是为了阻止美国太平洋舰队干预日军向东南亚的推进。联合舰队司令长官山本五十六力主此举，南云忠一中将率领的六艘航空母舰组成的机动部队分两波派出353架飞机。

第一波于星期日早上7时48分抵达。一枚炸弹引爆了战列舰“亚利桑那”号的前部弹药库，舰上1512人中有1177人丧生，是损失最惨重的一艘舰；“俄克拉何马”号倾覆，又有429人遇难。美国国家公园管理局统计共有2390名美国人死亡，其中49人为平民。日本损失29架飞机、五艘袖珍潜艇和约130人，来自其中一艘潜艇的海军少尉酒卷和男成为这场战争中第一名日本战俘。

这次袭击错过了最关键的目标：舰队的三艘航空母舰正在海上，油库、修船设施和潜艇基地都未受打击。罗斯福总统称12月7日是“一个永远蒙受耻辱的日子”，并于12月8日带领美国加入第二次世界大战。

name.zh: 珊瑚海海战

summary.en: US and Australian naval forces turned back a Japanese seaborne invasion of Port Moresby in New Guinea. In the first battle fought between aircraft carriers, the opposing fleets never sighted each other. Japan lost the light carrier Shōhō and the US the carrier Lexington, but the damage to two Japanese fleet carriers kept them out of Midway.
summary.zh: 美国与澳大利亚海军击退了日本经海路进攻新几内亚莫尔兹比港的企图。这是第一场航空母舰之间的海战，交战双方舰队始终未曾目视对方。日本损失轻型航母“祥凤”号，美国损失航母“列克星敦”号，但日本两艘舰队航母受损，因而未能参加中途岛海战。

story.en:
In spring 1942 Japan's Operation MO aimed to seize Tulagi in the Solomons for a seaplane base and to land troops at Port Moresby, the Allied base on the south coast of Papua, from which aircraft could reach northern Australia. The Americans sent two carriers, Lexington and Yorktown, under Rear Admiral Frank Jack Fletcher, joined by an Australian-American cruiser force under Rear Admiral John Crace.

On 7 May American aircraft sank the light carrier Shōhō, and a pilot radioed "Scratch one flat top!" Japanese planes sank the destroyer Sims and crippled the oiler Neosho, while Crace's cruisers, sent to block the Jomard Passage, were attacked from the air with little damage. On 8 May each side's carriers struck the other's: Shōkaku was badly hit, Yorktown damaged and Lexington so wrecked that she was scuttled.

Japan sank more ships, but the invasion convoy turned back. It was the first time a major Japanese advance had been stopped, and the damaged Shōkaku and Zuikaku, short of aircraft, missed Midway a month later. Australians long remembered it as the battle that saved their country.
story.zh:
1942年春，日本的“MO作战”旨在夺取所罗门群岛的图拉吉以建立水上飞机基地，并在巴布亚南岸的盟军基地莫尔兹比港登陆，从那里日机可以飞抵澳大利亚北部。美军派出“列克星敦”号和“约克城”号两艘航母，由弗兰克·杰克·弗莱彻少将指挥，另有约翰·克雷斯少将率领的澳美巡洋舰编队协同作战。

5月7日，美机击沉轻型航母“祥凤”号，一名飞行员在无线电中喊道：“干掉一艘平顶船！”日机击沉驱逐舰“西姆斯”号，重创油船“尼奥肖”号；奉命封锁乔马德水道的克雷斯巡洋舰编队遭到空袭，但损伤轻微。5月8日，双方航母互相攻击：“翔鹤”号遭重创，“约克城”号受损，“列克星敦”号则损毁严重，最终被自沉。

日本击沉的舰船更多，但入侵船队被迫折返。这是日军大规模攻势第一次被阻止，受损的“翔鹤”号和缺少飞机的“瑞鹤”号未能参加一个月后的中途岛海战。澳大利亚人长期把它铭记为拯救了国家的一战。
